content: The systemic exposure of fluticasone, when inhaled, can be increased by strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, such as ritonavir, due to their impact on hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This necessitates caution and close monitoring. Alternative therapies should be considered in cases of significant interaction risk. Ritonavir significantly increases the systemic levels of intranasal fluticasone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction can lead to systemic corticosteroid adverse effects, including signs and symptoms of Cushing's syndrome. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Lopinavir also increases the systemic levels of intranasal fluticasone via CYP3A4 inhibition. This interaction warrants avoiding coadministration or using alternative therapies. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors can elevate systemic corticosteroid concentrations, leading to adverse effects. Patients should be monitored for signs of high corticosteroid levels, such as Cushing-type symptoms. Ritonavir increases the toxicity of fluvastatin through mechanisms other than CYP3A4 inhibition. This interaction may elevate the risk of myopathy, necessitating caution and close monitoring. Fluvoxamine increases the levels of ritonavir and lopinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction requires caution and monitoring. Food enhances the gastrointestinal absorption of ritonavir, leading to increased systemic levels. This effect is specific to the oral form of ritonavir and is considered minor with unknown clinical significance. Fosamprenavir and ritonavir both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Fosamprenavir also increases the levels of ritonavir and lopinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Fosaprepitant increases the levels of ritonavir and lopinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Lopinavir also increases the levels of fosaprepitant. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Fosphenytoin decreases the levels of ritonavir and lopinavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and by acting on the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. This interaction requires caution and monitoring. Fostamatinib increases the levels of ritonavir by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Concomitant use may increase concentrations of P-gp substrates. Ritonavir also increases fostamatinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Lopinavir and fostemsavir both prolong the QTc interval. QTc prolongation has been reported with higher-than-recommended doses of fostemsavir. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Ritonavir increases the levels of futibatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration with drugs that are dual P-gp and strong CYP3A inhibitors may increase futibatinib toxicities. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Ganaxolone exposure changes when coadministered with CYP3A4 inhibitors are not expected to be clinically significant. However, caution and monitoring are advised. Garlic decreases ritonavir levels through an unknown mechanism. This interaction requires caution and monitoring. Lopinavir increases gefitinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Ritonavir also increases gefitinib levels through the same mechanism. Gemifloxacin and lopinavir both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Lopinavir and gemtuzumab both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ritonavir increases gentamicin levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are required. Lopinavir increases gepirone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Ritonavir also increases gepirone levels through the same mechanism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Gilteritinib and lopinavir both prolong the QTc interval. Ritonavir increases gilteritinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If unavoidable, closely monitor for gilteritinib-related adverse effects. Lopinavir and givinostat both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If unavoidable, obtain ECGs at baseline, during concomitant use, and as clinically indicated. Withhold therapy if the QTc interval exceeds 500 ms or if there is a change from baseline greater than 60 ms. Givosiran increases ritonavir levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If unavoidable, decrease the dosage of CYP2D6 substrates according to approved product labeling. Ritonavir increases glasdegib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Lopinavir also increases glasdegib levels through the same mechanism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If unavoidable, monitor for QTc prolongation. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases ritonavir levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Ritonavir increases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels by decreasing metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Lopinavir decreases the effects of glimepiride through mechanisms other than CYP3A4 inhibition. Ritonavir may increase or decrease glimepiride levels. Reports of hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance with protease inhibitors necessitate caution and monitoring. Lopinavir decreases the effects of glipizide through mechanisms other than CYP3A4 inhibition. Ritonavir may increase or decrease glipizide levels. Reports of hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance with protease inhibitors necessitate caution and monitoring. Lopinavir decreases the effects of glyburide through mechanisms other than CYP3A4 inhibition. Ritonavir may increase or decrease glyburide levels. Reports of hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance with protease inhibitors necessitate caution and monitoring. Goserelin increases lopinavir toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. This interaction increases the risk of torsades de pointes. Coadministration is contraindicated. Granisetron and lopinavir both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Grapefruit increases ritonavir and lopinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Griseofulvin decreases ritonavir and lopinavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. Ritonavir increases guanfacine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. FDA-approved labeling for extended-release guanfacine recommends halving the dosage when coadministered with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Ritonavir increases haloperidol levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Histrelin increases lopinavir toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. This interaction increases the risk of torsades de pointes. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Lopinavir increases hydrocodone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Ritonavir also increases hydrocodone levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Coadministration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may result in potentially fatal respiratory depression. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Ritonavir increases hydrocortisone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Hydrocortisone decreases ritonavir and lopinavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. Ritonavir increases hydromorphone levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and lopinavir both prolong the QTc interval. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and ritonavir also prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Ritonavir increases hydroxyprogesterone caproate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Lopinavir also increases hydroxyprogesterone caproate levels through the same mechanism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Hydroxyzine and lopinavir both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Ritonavir increases ibrutinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Lopinavir also increases ibrutinib levels through the same mechanism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor must be used short-term, interrupt ibrutinib therapy until the inhibitor is discontinued. Idelalisib increases lopinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Idelalisib is a strong CYP3A inhibitor; avoid coadministration with sensitive CYP3A substrates.
